The console might cost too much for you, but it's still sold out around the world. Someone is surely buying them.

About looks, I've never bought or avoided a console based on its looks. (Hell, I had a Game Gear. A Game Gear.) If anything comes up about looks, it should be the graphics of the games. I hear they're pretty spectacular.

Good games are a matter of opinion. While the number of good games can definitely make or break a console (see Sega Saturn, Nintendo 64, Dreamcast), it's still a matter of time before we know.

Blu-Ray is probably the biggest selling point of the PS3, and it's certainly the biggest point according to Sony. Games are one thing, but a $600 Blu-Ray player is something you can't get anywhere else. Again, you might not be the type to want this. You think they're too expensive in the first place. But for someone with an income (and maybe a plasma TV), a Blu-Ray player can be a nice accessory. And the Blu-Ray discs don't cost that much, by the way. Movies for $30, games for $60. (As opposed to $20 and $50 on DVD, respectively.)

Like looks of a console, the controller isn't something that's ever bothered me. The PS3 may not have a whole new form of interaction, but neither have any of the other consoles before this, and they were still fun. The Super Nintendo controller is just an NES one with four extra buttons. The Gamecube controller is just a mix of the Playstation and Dreamcast controllers. PS3 is a PS2 controller with tilt added. (And vibration is hardly even an issue. I could live without vibration.)
